HALTON & THE GREATER TORONTO AREA

Interior painting in Halton

A new colour is the visible change. The useful conversation starts with the surfaces underneath, the repairs needed, and which parts of the room belong in the job.

Describe your project

Jobs to discuss

Walls & ceilings

A room refresh or several spaces, with the areas to be painted and any existing defects recorded.

Trim & doors

Baseboards, door frames, and interior doors, with the finish and preparation discussed separately.

Preparation & repairs

Cleaning, patching, and surface preparation appropriate to the condition of the existing coating.

Put the preparation in writing

List the surfaces as well as the colour. Note peeling finishes, old patches, marks, and any wallpaper removal history. Agree on the repairs, protection, coating system, and access arrangements before comparing estimates.

  • Are walls, ceilings, trim, and doors all included?
  • Which existing defects should be repaired, and which will remain?
  • Who supplies the paint, and which colour and finish are intended?
  • What needs moving or protecting, and when can the room be accessed?

Before settling the scope

Older painted surfaces may contain lead. Identify the coating history and arrange an appropriate assessment before disturbing uncertain finishes. Health Canada: lead-based paint.

YOUR PROJECT BRIEF

What to include

  • Your city, the rooms, and approximate dimensions or a simple sketch.
  • The walls, ceilings, trim, and doors you want included.
  • Known surface issues, colour ideas, and practical access constraints.

For example

Refresh the bedroom walls and baseboards; leave the ceiling and doors. There are old fixing holes and two visible patches. Please identify preparation and painting separately.

Planning questions

Do I need to choose the colour before discussing the job?

You can start with the rooms and surfaces. Record the final colour and finish in the agreed scope before materials are selected and work is scheduled.

How many coats will be needed?

That depends on the existing surface and the selected coating system. Ask what preparation, primer, and finish coats the proposal includes rather than assuming one number fits every room.

When can I use the room again?

Discuss access and the selected product’s drying and curing guidance as part of planning. There is no single timetable that applies to every paint and room.
